reads: POST {apiBase}/core/i/{token}/address/list.json (while the main grant lists Address)
POST {apiBase}/core/i/{propertyToken}/introspect.json (only when the link carries #property-token=; any failure means no property is readable)
POST {apiBase}/core-rm/i/{propertyToken}/resource/list.json (only while the property grant introspects Resource as readable)
GET {apiBase}/core/image/{imageId}/get?width=440 (the provider logo, loaded by the browser as an image, without the token)

GET {apiBase}/core/media/{planId}/stream.json (an approved property plan named by its granted Resource's PROPERTY_PLAN, read anonymously on the contract details step while REVIEW_MAPS_API_KEY is set, without the token)
GET https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js?key={REVIEW_MAPS_API_KEY} (only while REVIEW_MAPS_API_KEY is set and only on the contract details step; the token never reaches Google)
api.token: read from the #token= fragment only; it appears in no query string, storage, console output or page markup, and reaches the clipboard only inside the page address, when the client presses Copy link
api.propertyToken: read from the #property-token= fragment only, beside #token=; it is the separate core-rm grant of the package's Resource rows, used for the property introspection and the Resource list and nothing else, and is kept out of queries, storage, console output and page markup like the main token

plannedFields.optionLabel: the Order's PRICING_MODEL while it still carries one; otherwise the NAME its lines' ProductPrice rows share, else the price type (PER_SERVICE when no price is recurrent, RECURRING when every one is) refined to MONTHLY or SEASONAL only by OrderItem.metadata INTERVAL_COUNT/INTERVAL_UNIT in MONTH (1 or more), else Option {n}
plannedFields.accountPrimaryEmail: contacts[type PRIMARY].contactEntries[type EMAIL].value when exactly one is returned, otherwise the Account attribute REPRESENTATIVE_EMAIL

constraints: Download PDF creates a local, selectable-text A4 copy of the normalized authorized view, including every quotation option or the agreement's parties, services and terms. It never exports a token, URL, unsent form or comment draft, recalculates money, or sends document data to another service. Partial reads disable export, duplicate clicks are single-flight, and a changed or revoked document is not downloaded after generation. The pinned jsPDF engine and Roboto font are embedded as data-URI scripts to avoid JTE interpreting the vendor's template literals; no library/font request leaves the page.
REVIEW_API_BASE_URL must be an absolute https origin without a path. Until it is set the page reports that it is not set up and sends nothing.

PORTAL_URL ships empty. When it is an absolute https address, the completion states offer an Open the customer portal link to it above and below the agreement, and the thank-you state after approval and a closed link offer it once; any other value is discarded and no link shows. The portal access text itself never depends on Account.user.

Copy link is offered on the quote review, contract details and agreement review steps, never on an approved agreement or a state card. It hands the browser's clipboard the address the page was opened with, #token= fragment included, when the client presses it, and sends it nowhere else. A browser that refuses the write leaves the client with the address bar and the provider's email. The link carries nothing the client typed: a returning client sees what the provider's system holds.
A link that closes after the details or the approval were sent ends on a thank-you card; a link that is closed when it is opened keeps the expired-or-withdrawn card.

An agreement awaiting approval offers Request changes beside Approve when the link delegates SENT_TO_CLIENT-CLIENT_CHANGES_REQUESTED. The client's text is sent as MESSAGE; an empty text is not sent. The link stays open, and while the agreement is CLIENT_CHANGES_REQUESTED it thanks the client, says the provider emails a new link, and shows the agreement as it was sent. A link issued before the change request existed offers approval alone.

Contact us closes every page that has read an agreement. It shows the agreement's PROVIDER_CONTACT_PHONE and PROVIDER_CONTACT_EMAIL, which the provider's workflow copies from the organization before it issues each link: a dialable number and a mail address become links, anything else is shown as text, and a missing value has no row. The agreement pages show the provider's logo from PROVIDER_LOGO, an image id; an agreement without one, or an image that fails to load, shows none.

REVIEW_MAPS_API_KEY ships empty; its value is the operator's, set in the page's PageContext. While it is empty or not a key the page loads no Google script, the billing address is a plain text field and no plan is shown. With a key, the contract details step loads the Maps JavaScript API once, offers Google address suggestions under the billing address, pins the chosen or typed address on a map (or says it was not found, and the client can still send it as written), and switches the document's referrer policy from no-referrer to strict-origin so Google can check the key against the page's origin; the #token= fragment is never part of a referrer.

The billing address is the client's own value. The contract details step offers each approved property's service address as a button that copies it into the billing field, where the client sees and can change it, and sends it as BILLING_ADDRESS like a typed address; nothing fills the billing field from a service address on its own.

A link may carry #property-token= beside #token=: a second grant, issued on core-rm, of one Resource per property of the package. The page introspects it and lists Resource with it, and lists Address with the main token. A link without it, or a property grant or Address read that fails for any reason (401 and 404 included), shows the page the main grant decides, with each property's address unavailable and no plan: it never closes the page, shows an error or retries for it.

A property's address is its granted Resource's ADDRESS id looked up among the granted Address rows, written as the backend writes addresses: address1, address2, city, jurisdiction, state.code, postalCode, country.id, each trimmed, empty parts and parts equal to an earlier one (ignoring case) skipped, joined with ", ", else the Address alias. An id that is missing or not among the granted rows gives no address.

Each approved property whose granted Resource names one plan in PROPERTY_PLAN (a MediaAsset id, or a one-entry media list) shows it on the contract details step while REVIEW_MAPS_API_KEY is set: the file is read anonymously from /core/media/{id}/stream.json, its GOOGLE_MAPS shapes are drawn read-only over a satellite map, and the page lists each element with the area on the plan in square feet, measured like the Plans editor and Approve Plan (local equirectangular projection, elevation ignored). Image overlays are not drawn. PROPERTY_PLAN_DRAFT is never read. Two different plans, an unreadable file or a file without a map shape show that the plan cannot be shown.
Every other parameter is copy. No token, account, order, document or customer value is a parameter.

While the agreement is CLIENT_DETAILS_RECEIVED the page re-reads it one read at a time after 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 15, 15, 15 s, then says the check is taking longer than usual and offers Refresh status. It stops re-reading as soon as the agreement leaves that state.
CLIENT_DETAILS_ERRORS reaches the client only as copy: a known code marks its field, PROCESSING_FAILED has its own notice, and an unknown code adds a generic line, never the code.
The document ships in live data mode with no fixtures. A data mode other than live finds no fixtures and reports that it is not set up; it never shows demonstration data.

Money is shown only as the server returns it: unit price as amount, quantity as itemCount, subtotal as totalCharges, taxes as totalTaxes and option total as grandTotal. A field the server does not return has no row; nothing is summed or multiplied in the browser.
Every command is single-flight per record and renders only the state read back afterwards; a refusal shows the server message and assumes nothing.
Markup is built with createElement and textContent; the runtime uses no innerHTML, eval or new Function, and terms are rendered as text blocks.
The theme is snow and the colour mode follows the viewer's prefers-color-scheme.
